No points. Just names.

There is no scoring system. Every player you name counts as exactly one, star or practice squad, and the only number that matters is how many people you get. The more, the better. Rarity does not change what a name is worth, it only changes how much time it buys you in All-Time.

All-Time Sprint: how the clock works

All-Time is a different game. You start with one 30-second clock for the entire run. It never resets between names and there are no lives: wrong and repeat guesses just burn seconds. Naming a player adds time back based on rarity, and only the rare ones add enough to matter. That is why a big All-Time number is almost impossible unless you go deep: the stars everyone knows add zero seconds, so a run built on big names dies at 30 seconds no matter how fast you type.

+0s
Rarity 1–34: stars and starters add no time
+1s
Rarity 35–59: role players
+2s
Rarity 60–79: real deep cuts
+4s
Rarity 80+: super rare, the only names that truly extend a run
+5s
Fan Favorite: biggest time bonus on the board

Tiers in All-Time are based on how many you name, not percent of the roster: Fan at 10, Ball Knower at 20, Expert at 35, Elite at 50, GOAT at 75.

Each mode hides its own Fan Favorite: a current cult favorite in Current mode, an all-time cult hero in All-Time mode. Current rosters are the full 2026 rosters including practice squads; All-Time rosters are the complete franchise lists, played as a 30-second sprint where rare names add time back. Naming the whole roster ends the game early, in a good way.
